question.problem:
Which of the following vector-valued functions are differentiable with respect to $t$ on $t\in (\pi ,2\pi )?$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨{sin}^{2}⁡t,\,\frac{1}{t},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨t\sqrt{t},\,1-{t}^{2},\,t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩ \\ h(t) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,2t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
All of these vector-valued functions are defined for all  $t\in (\pi ,2\pi ).$ 

A function is differentiable on the interval $(\pi ,2\pi )$ if and only if each of its component functions is differentiable on that interval. 

Let's now consider the functions one-by-one.

- We differentiate $f(t)$ to find ${f}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({sin}^{2}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since each component of ${f}^{′}(t)$ is defined for all  $t\in (\pi ,2\pi )$, we conclude that $f(t)$ is differentiable on this interval.

- Next, we differentiate $g(t)$ to find ${g}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\sqrt{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3/2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{2}{t}^{1/2},\,-2t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+2t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{t},\,-2t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+2t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since each component of  ${g}^{′}(t)$ is defined for all  $t\in (\pi ,2\pi )$, we have that $g(t)$ is differentiable on this interval.

- Finally, we differentiate $h(t)$ to find ${h}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,2,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since each component of  ${h}^{′}(t)$ is defined for all $t\in (\pi ,2\pi )$, we conclude that $h(t)$ is differentiable on this interval.

Therefore, the answer is: 

$\,$ All the functions are differentiable on $(\pi ,2\pi ).$
